title: Speech group meeting: acoustic model ablations (excerpt)

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: Okay, let's get going. It's Thursday, um, second of April. We have, what, forty minutes? So the agenda is the ablation results, the workshop paper, and then logistics.

transcript.speaker: Wen Li
transcript.text: Sounds good.

transcript.speaker: Tomas Eriksson
transcript.text: Fine by me.

transcript.speaker: Aisha Khan
transcript.text: Can everyone see the slides? I'll, um, share the, the first table.

transcript.speaker: Wen Li
transcript.text: Yes, I see it.

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: So where are we on the baseline?

transcript.speaker: Wen Li
transcript.text: So the baseline word error rate is, um, eleven point four on the dev set. But I think it's, it's not quite right, because the language model I used is the old one.

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: The old one from the last paper?

transcript.speaker: Wen Li
transcript.text: Yeah. The new one has the extra web text and it should drop, I'd guess, by half a point.

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: Then it's not a fair baseline. Wen, rerun it with the new language model.

transcript.speaker: Wen Li
transcript.text: Yes, I'll rerun the baseline with the new language model. It's about a day of compute. I can have it by Monday.

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: Monday the sixth, good.

transcript.speaker: Wen Li
transcript.text: Yeah.

transcript.speaker: Aisha Khan
transcript.text: And is it the full training set or the subset?

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: That was the other question. Tomas?

transcript.speaker: Tomas Eriksson
transcript.text: So the full set takes five days per run and we have, like, twelve ablations. The three hundred hour subset is eight hours per run and the ranking of the systems was the same in my pilot.

transcript.speaker: Aisha Khan
transcript.text: The ranking was the same? Completely?

transcript.speaker: Tomas Eriksson
transcript.text: For the top five, yes. Below that there was some noise.

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: Then I'm happy. Subset for the ablations, and the full set only for the final numbers. Everyone agree?

transcript.speaker: Wen Li
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Aisha Khan
transcript.text: Agreed.

transcript.speaker: Tomas Eriksson
transcript.text: Yeah.

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: Good, three hundred hours for all ablations. Decided.

transcript.speaker: Tomas Eriksson
transcript.text: One thing about the data, there's the segmentation issue. About ten percent of the utterances are cut in the middle of words.

transcript.speaker: Aisha Khan
transcript.text: That would affect the alignments.

transcript.speaker: Tomas Eriksson
transcript.text: Yeah, definitely. So I'm going to re-segment the corpus before we train anything.

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: How long does that take?

transcript.speaker: Tomas Eriksson
transcript.text: Um, it's a script, it should be a couple of hours. I'll just do it.

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Aisha Khan
transcript.text: And then I'll need the aligned data for the, for the pronunciation analysis. Can you send it to me?

transcript.speaker: Tomas Eriksson
transcript.text: Sure. I'll send the aligned data to you by the ninth. Is that okay?

transcript.speaker: Aisha Khan
transcript.text: The ninth is Thursday. That's fine.

transcript.speaker: Wen Li
transcript.text: What about the tokenizer? Do we retrain it on the new text?

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: I'd rather not. It changes everything downstream. Keep the current tokenizer.

transcript.speaker: Wen Li
transcript.text: Okay, keep it.

transcript.speaker: Aisha Khan
transcript.text: So that's a decision, no retraining of the tokenizer?

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: Yes. We keep the current tokenizer and we don't retrain it.

transcript.speaker: Tomas Eriksson
transcript.text: I was going to say, if we had unlimited GPUs we would train the big model on everything. But, we don't.

transcript.speaker: Wen Li
transcript.text: Ha. If we had unlimited GPUs I'd be on holiday.

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: Let's stay on topic.

transcript.speaker: Aisha Khan
transcript.text: What about the low-resource condition? The numbers are really bad there.

transcript.speaker: Wen Li
transcript.text: Yeah. Um, maybe we should try wav2vec features for that. I read a paper where they get a big gain at ten hours.

transcript.speaker: Tomas Eriksson
transcript.text: That's interesting. Could be.

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: It's a good thought. I don't want to commit anyone to it before we see the baseline.

transcript.speaker: Wen Li
transcript.text: Right, that's fair. I was just throwing it out.

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: Okay. The workshop. The deadline is the first week of May, so, Aisha, are you able to write the abstract?

transcript.speaker: Aisha Khan
transcript.text: I should be able to draft the abstract by the end of the month. It depends on whether the reviews for the other paper come back, so, I'll try.

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: End of the month, April thirtieth. Okay.

transcript.speaker: Aisha Khan
transcript.text: Yes, that's the plan, as far as I can tell.

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: Now logistics. The seminar room for the next group meeting is double booked on the, uh, the usual day.

transcript.speaker: Wen Li
transcript.text: Again?

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: Yes. I'll email the department about the seminar room and sort it out.

transcript.speaker: Tomas Eriksson
transcript.text: Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: And, um, GPUs. Who has the GPU allocation for next week? Because the cluster is being shared with the vision group and someone has to book it.

transcript.speaker: Wen Li
transcript.text: I thought Tomas had it.

transcript.speaker: Tomas Eriksson
transcript.text: No, I had it last week.

transcript.speaker: Aisha Khan
transcript.text: I don't have a login for the booking system.

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: Hm. Okay, so, nobody. That needs a name.

transcript.speaker: Wen Li
transcript.text: Hm.

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: I'll leave it open for now, we'll see on Monday.

transcript.speaker: Tomas Eriksson
transcript.text: By the way, I'll be redoing the segmentation of the corpus today actually, it's running already, so I'll segment the corpus again with the fix.

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: That is the same thing as before, Tomas. Fine.

transcript.speaker: Tomas Eriksson
transcript.text: Yeah, sorry. Same.

transcript.speaker: Aisha Khan
transcript.text: Did anyone see the new keynote speaker list?

transcript.speaker: Wen Li
transcript.text: Not yet. Is it good?

transcript.speaker: Aisha Khan
transcript.text: It's the usual suspects.

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: Okay. If there's nothing else, thank you everyone.

transcript.speaker: Wen Li
transcript.text: Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Tomas Eriksson
transcript.text: Bye.

transcript.speaker: Aisha Khan
transcript.text: Bye all.

transcript.speaker: Prof Ramos
transcript.text: And remember the, uh, the reading group is cancelled this week.

transcript.speaker: Wen Li
transcript.text: Okay, noted.

decisions.text: Use the 300-hour subset for all the ablations
Keep the current tokenizer and do not retrain it
